spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates predefined-entity and numeric-reference decoding, CDATASection nodes (nodeType 4) with literal content, and internal-DTD entity expansion — each against the real parser output, matching XML 1.0 sections 4.6/2.7.

interactive.rationale: Five presets plus free editing with parse-on-input; resolved textContent, code-unit/code-point lengths, and a per-node table all update live.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card's promise matches the verified page behaviour.

edge_cases.rationale: Fixed in this refile: the v151 explanation claimed browsers do not expand general DTD entities, but the DTD preset observably expands the internal-subset entity to 'Hello, world!' — the copy now distinguishes internal-subset expansion (allowed) from external entities (the XXE boundary, refused per Chromium's XMLNoExternalEntities) and expansion caps for billion-laughs.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry plus the exact XML spec sections the page demonstrates.

conformance.rationale: The new v153 feature suite (extending the v151 one with XHR-responseXML and SVG-as-image scenario checks) ran 7 pass / 0 fail / 0 blocked in the verification browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP page-driver run (headless Chromium 141): predefined preset resolved to 'Tom & Jerry say \"hi\" <loudly> & often'; CDATA preset produced a nodeType-4 row with literal '<' and '&'; DTD preset expanded to 'Hello, world!' — the observation that drove the copy fix; console/network clean; screenshot v153-xml-ent.png read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts xml-entities-parsed with the wellFormed flag and resolved length on every parse.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; status chips put ivory text on the emerald/rose accents (both >4.4:1); tables and code blocks scroll in their own containers.

accessibility.rationale: Status chip role=status aria-live=polite; panels are headed; the node table has an aria-label and headers; textarea labelled.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: deno task responsive-check v153/xml-parsing-in-rust-for-non-xslt-scenarios --no-server: desktop OK clean, mobile OK (sub-44px flags are inline links; textareas, selects, and buttons remain usable); both screenshots read and judged clean.

openQuestions.title: Re-run these contract demos with the Rust parser active
openQuestions.detail: The verification browser runs the current default engine. Launch with --enable-blink-features=XMLRustForNonXslt (or a Chrome 153 build after the flip) and confirm every preset — including parsererror text, entity expansion, and namespace resolution — behaves identically, which is the feature's whole compatibility promise. Any observable difference would be a Chromium bug worth filing.

openQuestions.title: Compare internal-DTD entity behaviour across engines once the Rust parser is on
openQuestions.detail: Internal-subset entity expansion is an area where the Rust xml crate could plausibly differ from libxml2. After enabling XMLRustForNonXslt, run the dtd preset and record whether &who; still expands to 'world' — a difference here would be exactly the kind of compatibility finding this feature's rollout needs.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Let two-pane editors stack on narrow viewports and keep tables/code scrolling in their own container.

summary: v153 refile fixing a factual error in the v151 copy: internal-DTD-subset entities ARE expanded by the browser (observed live: 'Hello, world!'), and the security boundary is external entities (XXE) plus expansion caps — the page now says so precisely, citing XMLNoExternalEntities. Verified via CDP headless Chromium 141 with a clean console.
